environmentalPersistence: Low to moderate — degrades via photolysis and microbial hydrolysis within days

morphologicalEffects.heightSuppression: Moderate — SA signaling antagonizes gibberellin-mediated elongation
morphologicalEffects.chlorosis: Mild — less than MeJA; SA primarily activates defense rather than degrading chlorophyll
morphologicalEffects.necrosis: Moderate at high doses — hypersensitive response-like lesions
morphologicalEffects.pigmentation: Very strong — SA drives anthocyanin biosynthesis strongly in Coleus; near MeJA levels
morphologicalEffects.newVsOldLeaves: Young leaves show pigmentation first; lesions form on mid-age leaves

physiologyEffects.stomatalConductance: Decreased — SA-mediated ABA crosstalk promotes closure

molecularEffects.oxidativeStress: Moderate — SA-triggered oxidative burst is part of hypersensitive response
molecularEffects.anthocyaninInduction: Very strong — among strongest anthocyanin inducers in Coleus

microbiomeEffects.beneficialBacteriaEffect: Some PGPR suppressed; SA-producing bacteria may increase
microbiomeEffects.fungalEffect: Pathogenic fungi suppressed via induced systemic resistance

temporalDynamics.sensitization: Strong priming — MeSA exposure induces systemic acquired resistance; second exposure triggers faster, stronger response

visualSimulation.colorChanges: Green → deep red-purple (anthocyanin); small necrotic lesions at high doses
visualSimulation.firstAffectedRegion: Young apical leaves for pigmentation; mid-canopy for lesions
visualSimulation.damagePattern: Patchy necrotic spots on otherwise deeply pigmented leaves
visualSimulation.heatmapGlow: Very strong — second only to MeJA in anthocyanin signal; SA-glucoside adds secondary peak
visualSimulation.microbiomeParticles: Mildly reduced diversity; pathogen fraction decreased
visualSimulation.recoveryVisual: Good — pigmentation fades, lesion scars remain

synergies.synergyNote: MeSA + MeJA is the strongest pigmentation/defense combo in the simulator — both pathways converge on anthocyanin biosynthesis and PR proteins simultaneously
synergies.antagonismNote: SA and ET/JA pathways have complex crosstalk; SA can suppress JA/ET-mediated necrosis in some contexts

educationalContext.realWorldSources: Wintergreen plants, birch bark, many flowering plants under pathogen attack; aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid) is a derivative
educationalContext.agriculturalUse: Studied as a biocontrol agent; used in SAR (systemic acquired resistance) research
educationalContext.humanToxicity: Low at ambient concentrations; toxic in large doses (related to aspirin toxicity)
educationalContext.climateLink: MeSA emissions increase under heat and pathogen stress — relevant to changing disease pressure under climate change
educationalContext.indoorOutdoor: Both — wintergreen products indoors; natural plant emissions outdoors
educationalContext.whyStudentsCare: Aspirin comes from this molecule — the connection between plant defense chemistry and one of the world's most common medicines is immediately engaging
educationalContext.realWorldIssue: Natural disease resistance, sustainable agriculture, pharmaceutical origins
